I'm 66, been farming these 10 mu since I was 16. My wife and I manage the place, though our child works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for busy seasons. We're not young anymore, so I have to be careful with my back and my wallet.

I run wheat-maize double cropping on about 6 mu — that's the core of my farm. I know this system like the back of my hand. I also keep 3 mu of cotton and a little over 1 mu of stevia on the side. The cotton is hard work but brings decent cash, and the stevia… well, someone at the market suggested it two years ago, and it's been alright.

**Wheat** — I'll plant around October 10th with the same improved variety I've been using. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, and the year before was better. I'm hoping for 420 kg this time if the weather cooperates. I'll put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — the shop has 15-15-15 — and then topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. That's usually around Qingming. I'll irrigate three times: at planting, at jointing, and at flowering. Water from the well isn't cheap anymore with the meters, so I watch it, but wheat can't go thirsty at jointing.

**Maize** — goes in right after wheat harvest, usually June 8th to 10th. The window is tight — sometimes I hire the custom planter to get it in fast. I buy hybrid seed every year, can't save it. Fertilizer goes down with the planter, about 40 jin of compound per mu, and I'll add urea when the maize is knee-high. Irrigate once or twice, depending on the rain. If July is wet, maybe just once.

**Cotton** — planted in late April with plastic mulch. I need to watch for bollworm — last year wasn't too bad. I'll fertilize three times: base, flowering, and when the bolls are setting. The problem with cotton is the picking. My wife and I can do some, but for the main picking we need hired hands. That's my biggest labor cost. I'm expecting maybe 260 kg of lint per mu if the weather holds.

**Stevia** — just on 1.1 mu. It's not like the grain crops — I harvest it two or three times through the summer. Doesn't need much, just some fertilizer and water. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress after the first cut.

I'm watching my money carefully. Seed, fertilizer, water, pesticides, plus hired labor for wheat harvest and cotton picking — it'll come to about 8,200 yuan. That's a lot for us. I'm not trying to get the highest yield in the village; I'm trying to make sure we don't lose money and have enough to eat. If prices are good, maybe I'll do a bit better next year. If not, I'll cut back somewhere.
